en: A zombie dog. Humans have so much needless wisdom that turning zombie seems to strip them of everything, but those with little intellect to begin with act much as they did in life. Zombie Fangs are no exception: they're said to gnaw Skeleton bones for fun.

A woman who died in childbirth or grieving a stillbirth is said to become a Langsuir. With a mouth on the back of her head she drinks blood and, perhaps from regret, preys only on children. Killing another's child won't bring hers back. Surely she knows...

A burly Skeleton infused with power, so big it is little different from a giant. Many Skeletons go into it, so when a Girou is smashed, the shards return to Skeleton form. After a Girou falls, vast numbers of Skeletons are said to lie strewn about.

A vampiress ensnaring prey with bewitching beauty, craving young women. Unlike rough lesser vampires, she draws her victim close by the waist, speaks of love, and waits till its eyes melt with bliss. Those charmed by her sweet kiss offer up their blood.

A sharp scythe that reaps heads in one sweep, a skull foretelling death, a vile centipede's body. You freeze, and suddenly every ally but you is dead... with this monster, that's commonplace. If you meet one, curse yourself for wandering into such a place.

One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of earth. Spirits are not harmful, but act by their own laws, so you may offend one unknowingly. It is not that strong, but if one attacks you, pay close attention to why it did.

A mountain fairy who grows turnips. It hands out turnip and radish seeds to children but is unwelcome, so it is always grumpy. Its sack, naturally, holds turnip seeds, radish seeds and such. Its hobby is strolling about counting the turnips it has grown.

One of the four great elements of all things: the elemental of wind. As if to say "nothing in this world stays the same," it keeps changing the land. Yet even a wind spirit stops now and then. If the wind suddenly dies on an adventure, one may be near.

A fairy said to know where gold, silver and treasure lie. It looks stubborn, but rumor says it is a timid old man. Also a shoemaker, it makes shoes for every race from fairies to giants. When a traveler's shoes break, it seems to pop up and mend them.

It appears before you out of nowhere. Speak and it won't answer; stare and you can't make out its form. A higher being's fragment, a demon in a god's guise, mere weather... Many tales are told, but lately some whisper it may be "a warning of some kind."

A strange light drifting in many places, also called a ghost light. Reach for it carelessly and the strange waves from its glowing body will freeze you in place. Its stamina is modest, but neither magic nor physical attacks work well on it: a tough foe.

An elemental that rules darkness. It moves through shadows, wandering in search of deeper dark. Being kin to the spirits, it is normally very docile, but the miasma of evil can drive it to attack people. If you see one, you would do well to keep away.

A lovely woman of the snowy peaks, with translucent white skin and a bewitching smile. Cold inside too, her breath never turns white: that's how to tell her from a normal woman. Rumors range from her killing the lost in the snow to her marrying for love.

Legend says a carefully made snowman gains a heart and helps mind children until it melts in spring. But if its heart goes unnoticed and it is neglected, loneliness draws an evil will, and it becomes a fiend freezing children to keep them by it forever.

A spirit that rules all four great elements of all things. A union of fire, water, earth and wind, it embodies the balance of magic that dwells in the world. When that balance breaks, it is said to appear to restore the world to its rightful form.

A fearsome coconut crab. In the forest it comes at you openly, snapping branches as it goes. Slow but hard to stop, it is very dangerous when several surround you. It has instinctive cunning too, good at driving prey into dead ends, so handle it with care.

A giant centipede that coils around a shield and lives in it like a hermit crab. Its defense is already tough, yet it hardens its allies further with spells. Some adventurers mistake the centipede for the shield's decoration and pay dearly for it.

Cordyceps are fungi that take over larvae in the soil; the true body is the plant part. But in this rare cordyceps the host also lives on in symbiosis. The flower gathers the tiny flying bugs that serve as food, and the insect preys on them.

Not content with scurrying, they now even fly. The terror of having one leap at you is beyond imagining. They have nests, which you may find on your adventures. If so, the wise move is to leave quietly. Poke one for fun, and a black terror will engulf you.

A strange creature that seizes prey with two oddly shaped jaws. The accordion-like, arm-shaped upper jaw is stronger than it looks; once it gets a firm grip, even a human can hardly escape. If you hear a grating "bzzzt," you had best be on your guard.

A mighty queen bee. It often rules a corner of the forest and shows no mercy to those who run wild in its territory, so take care not to upset it. Being a bee, it adores nectar; at harvest time it is seen flying about merrily in search of flowers itself.

A bird known for its chunky body and lovable face. Its tiny wings can't fly, but in exchange it gained legs to run on the ground. Its lower-body muscles are so developed it is round all over, hence the name meat bomb. Its meat is muscly, so tastes vary.

An odd animal that walks on its nose, balancing with its tail. Standing, it reaches a person's waist; its body is surprisingly big. It is docile, but when angered it casts the spell Zeo Nadar. If you meet a group of them, why not settle things peacefully?

In the pitch-black world of the deep sea, the vivid fins it suddenly spreads catch the eye. But this is nothing less than a declaration of war. It circles you seeking an opening to attack, yet endless carefree adventurers think they are being welcomed.

Tyrant of the forest: a menace that runs about on its huge body, mowing down trees. It needs a long run-up to start "running," but then won't stop, and is fairly fast. Meet one while camping and there's no time to save your gear: beat it or lose your gear.

Emperor Birds are very intelligent and once had fairly friendly ties with people. But since their delicious eggs were hailed as one of the Three Great Delicacies, endless overhunting has soured relations. Their bonds are strong; a long fight is dangerous.

A lizard full of poison. If its claws merely graze you, venom seeps in and eats at your whole body. Keep your distance, then? When its claws can't reach, a basilisk attacks with deadly poison breath. After the fight, you'll surely be drenched in poison.

Glittering wings and a gorgeous crest: a lavish mythical beast, yet it cannot fly. But who needs flight with an inborn power to petrify? Not just its attacks but its breath can turn you to stone. Take it lightly and you'll be a stone statue in no time.

A demon beast writhing slickly amid water columns. With an allure only inhuman women have, it draws adventurers in defenseless though they know it's a monster. Supple, mighty tentacles snare them, and the fanged lower mouth, not the upper, swallows them.

A beauty with a snake's body. Intelligent, she seldom attacks people, but things like "magic pools" can make her drunk and violent. Rumor says a child born of love with a lamia will have rare magic and be able to command every mythical beast.

A fox that lived long and gained mystic powers. Some take human form to beguile the powerful; others shun people in tiny mountain shrines. Angered, it calls heavenly winds and black clouds and strikes with eerie lightning. Proud, but fried tofu undoes it.

A divine sea fish shining with holy light. Any beast this huge should be slow, yet maybe thanks to the light magic it wears, it races about at baffling speed. So adventurers keep dying, unable to keep their distance or thrown off their usual rhythm.

A ghost that loves pranks, from cute ones like flying plates or doors that open and shut, to dangerous ones like flying weapons and blades. Sometimes it wants someone to notice something, so if you scold it and hear it out, you might become friends.

Novice servants forever make clumsy blunders. Fine if you can laugh it off, but some cost a life. The Ghost Maid is one such soul. Unaware she died, she still busily cleans for her master. Rumor says an even clumsier maid hasn't noticed her coworker died.

An odd spirit with a tube-shaped body whose end crosses into itself. Follow its outside with your eyes and you're inside; follow the inside and you're back outside. Normal to higher-dimensional beings, but if we try to grasp it, at worst we go mad.

When a Valkyrie dies, her god normally calls her soul to its rightful place. But some, rejected for deeds in life like breaking commandments, wander with nowhere to go. A weak heart seeks a god's salvation, and is rejected for that weakness. How sad.

A skull that swims through the air like a ray. Usually it glides lazily just above the ground, like a ray in the sea, but once it spots prey, it closes in on your feet at terrifying speed without a sound, then leaps up to strike all at once.

A vengeful dog spirit made by the curse kodoku. Inugami are said to be passed down in certain bloodlines for generations, often cited as proof that ordinary people, animals and plants can be drawn into dark arts. How sad, to find no freedom even in death.

King of the evil spirits. At this level, it no longer lingers in this world because it is lost, but by its own will. Spirits are everywhere, many of them souls with nowhere to go. The king summons such spirits as servants, making its position rock solid.

A female knight who lives in darkness. One thrust of her matchless spear sends frail spellcasters to the grave. 'Valkyrie' means a battle maiden blessed by the gods, yet she is a demon Valkyrie. If even demons serve a god, what manner of being is it?

A male dream demon flaunting a lewd symbol. Incubi prefer violating from within with words over the body, digging up desires prey hides and can tell no one. Once in their arms, normal acts never satisfy you; you roam unfulfilled, devouring body after body.

A demon who leads adventurers astray with her bewitching form. Even veterans can't handle the Succubus, in more ways than one. Her level drain is a menace. And yet... having your hard-won experience sucked away in sweet dreams... isn't that a fine life?

A savage she-demon smashing all with great claws. Famed for cruelty, she torments lovely prey hardest till it breaks. Ramming claws down the throats of pleading prey to force gags, peering at faces warped by terror, wet with tears and snot: her routine.

A demon embodying the underworld's flames. It holds 1,024 legions and leads Demon Valkyries and Hell Masters. Unusually for a demon, it wields priest spells calling down divine miracles. If the gods guarantee our justice, who proves the gods' justice?

A monstrous woman whose gaze turns onlookers to stone with terror. Not only her petrifying spells but her normal attacks are fierce. Few have seen her, but they say that when she laid down her arms, her eyes held a sorrow, as if longing for days gone by.

A two-headed dragon whose tail is also a head. Strong against attacks from all sides, it assails adventurers with balanced offense and defense. The two heads get along well. Coiled up asleep with both heads side by side, it is surprisingly adorable.

A dragon that hates having its back seen or being taken from behind. But it moves so sluggishly that it is always sad. All a Grannada can do is turn its head and glare bitterly with its one eye. The wistful nursery rhyme 'Behind the Grannada' is famous.

A mighty wyvern clutching a natural emerald. Its magic is superb too: besides dragon attacks, it deftly showers foes with magic light amplified by the emerald. It prefers emeralds but may take diamonds or rubies. Some are seen fighting over one emerald.

A samurai with no master. Origins vary: some lost their lord, others roamed alone as they pleased from the start. Wanderers they may be, but their skill is real. Take them lightly and you'll become 'rust on the katana,' or whatever it is they call it.

Warriors who train their bodies to the limit and crush foes with their own strength. Their fighting ability is truly remarkable. Their well-built muscles seem a point of pride; if they're friendly, they'll show off their physique without holding back.

A warrior fused with a chariot by alchemy. It turns tighter than it looks, and a head-on charge is hard to take well. Nor is fleeing easy: escape onto mountain trails or other unpaved roads, and it swaps its wheels for spiked ones and gives chase.

A female fighter who dearly loves to fight. Taking no lover, she sates every desire by driving her fists into others' bodies. Her whole body is a weapon; she excels at close combat. Want to writhe in agony from her passionate gut blow? Charge right in.

A samurai with the honored duty of raising the war banner, the army's symbol, in battle. In peacetime they also advise on domestic affairs, so are rather intellectual. Perhaps from handling the real work, their skill reportedly beats their lord's at times.

A lord of a land far east, on a stacked cushion called a 'zabutoon.' This lord crushes foes with political clout, not brawn, and lewdly calls women over when possible. Sweets set on gold coins somehow delight this lord, so bring some to get friendly.

A samurai who has mastered the finest skills. In master hands even a nameless katana is deadly. Take it away, and a lightning-fast dagger still slashes you deep in the side. A living legend of many tales. If you face it, show what today's living can do.

Sorceresses among the Witches who mastered higher magic through further training. Maybe everyone gets this way with room to breathe, but High Sorceresses are generally refined. Leading junior Witches, they giggle as they toy with adventurers using magic.

Wielders of more advanced alchemy, with a wider range of spells. At the intermediate level of alchemy, they begin to take an interest in 'the birth of life' as research. Creating life is dogged by 'bioethics,' but will that ever reach their ears?

Third-years about to graduate, writhing in a storm of remedial classes. The Academy values tradition and pride, so without real skill you're soon held back. Some fake it with magic, but teachers usually see through it and hold them back. Plan your studies.

Third-years about to graduate. Afterward, some will join the palace Magic Bureau, some will aid small farm villages as mages, others will seek deeper knowledge. What kind of mages will they become as they leave the nest? May happiness be theirs.

One who has completed the full course of alchemical study. She has even created the artificial life 'Homunculus'; all that remains is the Philosopher's Stone. People with a goal seem full of life, and this old woman is no exception: she looks very spry.

A mage of unknown identity in a clown's guise. It loves death and decadent games, and once its curiosity is sated, it gives a shrill, strange laugh. All wonder at its true face; none has seen it. Popping in and out of nowhere, it may not even be human.

A priestly calling from a land far to the east. With strange paper and sticks, they fight undead monsters, spirits among them. But as foes, fear their 'Barrier': it reflects most spells, so a party that relies solely on spells will struggle.

Head maid of the labyrinth. With calm judgment and precise action, she meets her master's every wish; her planner holds his schedule in detail. Leave it to her and all is well, but she's inflexible, hence strict. In battle, her fierce kicks crush his foes.

The strongest, most evil pontiff, who cast off self and gave his soul to evil. He wished his soul his god's slave; his self is nearly gone, his deeds bound by its doctrine. Never doubting, he seems a puppet. Perhaps this is a form of 'ultimate happiness'.

Appears at night and downs prey in the dark. Its aim earned it the name of one who could shoot down the moon. In 'Periatif', it is Jenas, Polyte's rival. The scene of their arrows colliding over the moon on the lake, sparks flying, has even been painted.

A beastfolk girl with skunk blood. Maybe it's her skunk nature, but when worked up, she gasses. When angry, of course, but also happy or sad; any feeling sets her off. So she is shunned, friendless and lonely. And then, feeling lonely, she gasses again.

A spider-like enchantress. Near her rear she spins sticky thread to snare prey, hard to cut and hard to escape. But she has a weak spot: thrust an arm into the spinneret and rip out the thread's source to wear Taranti down. Not that she'll let you easily.

A beautiful monster, human above and fish below. Trespass in their waters and they come in groups to drive you out. For all their aggression, they are said to be keenly interested in romance. When they drive off a gentleman, they sigh among the waves.

A cute-looking beastfolk girl who hunts those who stray into the woods. Ask her in turn, 'Why are your hands so hairy?' 'Why do your eyes gleam so?' 'Why are there fangs in your mouth?' She answers politely, edging closer step by step with a hidden knife.

A girl born to a tiger and a human, who thinks she's a tiger. Get near with ulterior motives and she'll surely bite, taking you for food. Catlike, she rubs her face very hard before rain. But go near thinking 'Aww, cute!' and you'll still be eaten.

Queen of the mermaids, ruler of the sea. In hand she holds a special spear, the 'Holy Sea Trident', and strikes intruders with lightning. She usually sits deep in the sea, but on calm full-moon nights she leads the mermaids to the surface for a feast.

A dread lord who has lost reason and swings his sword at friend and foe. No longer human, he is a mad beast. Yet by chance even a Raver Lord may regain his senses. Then, unable to bear his sins, he tries to destroy himself... dragging those near along.

A giant with three faces. The top one thinks, the second moves the arms, the third the legs. Cheerful, it befriends anyone, but after a while its pushy nature starts to show. In a good mood, it can be seen racing over hills and fields with a booming laugh.

A giant girl who lives in the sea. Despite her huge body, she is shy and bashful. When a tsunami she caused by moving heads for ships or fishing villages, she frets it will take small lives (which makes more tsunamis). Her dream is to be a lovely bride.

A wounded giant was treated by a passing priest and, deeply moved, began training as a priest too: the Cosplay Priest. But not knowing how to train, it just swings a club while shouting spell names it picked up. Someone should guide it, don't you think?

Once a female spirit ruling the sky, she grew close to a wind spirit and made the other spirits jealous. As a result, she was dragged from the sky to the ground. Her longing for the sky remains, but now she drifts over the land as one of the wind spirits.

The grand professor taking on challengers at the Magical Party! Whistle in mouth, the prof will tweet-tweet everyone's magic away! Show amazing magic and maybe you'll get something good~!? Prof. Rombino is the prof's half-sibling: same mom, different dad!
